resource_manager.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 56 bindable of 64 functions bound; the 8 _w wide-char variants are excluded project-wide. Covers the manager itself, its job queue, and all three data types (data_buffer, data_stream and the unified data_source). Tests drive the manager with job_thread_count=0 and the non-blocking flag and pump the queue explicitly, which makes a family built around asynchrony deterministic. ma_resource_manager_get_log returns a log pointer and ma_job is a struct, neither with a safe Mojo home: the log binds as whether one is present, and the job queue binds through a single job slot the shim keeps on the manager handle, so next_job / post_job / process_job are all reachable without Mojo holding an ma_job. ma_resource_manager_data_source_map and _unmap are exported by miniaudio but missing from its public header, so the shim declares them rather than leaving the pair unbound. Four behaviours are pinned by tests: (1) streams need a job thread -- data_stream_uninit always posts a free job and waits for it with no flag to opt out, so on a zero-thread manager a stream can be created but never torn down, since the calling thread is blocked inside uninit and cannot pump; (2) the non-blocking flag is only valid with zero job threads and is rejected with MA_INVALID_ARGS otherwise; (3) next_job reports MA_CANCELLED for a quit job -- the job struct is still filled, MA_CANCELLED is the label, not a failure -- and a quit job is sticky so process_next_job keeps reporting it, while process_job returns MA_SUCCESS because the cancel signal belongs to retrieval rather than execution; (4) mapping is streaming-only, answering MA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED on a decoded buffer. 17 binding + 9 API tests.

node.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 23 of 23 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_node_init takes a caller-supplied vtable and a Mojo function cannot cross the FFI boundary as a function pointer on this toolchain (the constraint the device family documents), so the shim owns a concrete node: an offset node that adds a constant to its input bus. It carries MA_NODE_FLAG_CONTINUOUS_PROCESSING | MA_NODE_FLAG_ALLOW_NULL_INPUT so it keeps producing with nothing attached -- without those a node with an unattached input bus is skipped entirely -- which makes it usable as a source and makes graph reads assertable. Chains are observable: two offset nodes in series produce twice the offset. Every node handle in the shim is one tagged-union allocation whose payloads all start with a ma_node_base, so attach_output_bus can target any node family without casting one handle type to another. ma_node_get_node_graph is bound as an identity question (does this node belong to that graph). NOTE for API users: a node's attachment lives only as long as the node value, and Mojo destroys a value after its last use, so a source touched only at attach time is gone before the read. 12 binding + 10 API tests.

data_source.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 30 of 30 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_data_source is an abstract vtable interface, so the shim owns the concrete implementation -- a buffer data source over an f32 PCM buffer copied into the handle at init (config_init + init + uninit) -- making the whole generic surface reachable with no device, engine, or file. Covers read/seek (read_pcm_frames, seek_pcm_frames, seek_to_pcm_frame, seek_seconds, seek_to_second), format/position/length queries in both frames and seconds, looping, range and loop point, and chaining (set/get current + next). get_current/get_next are bound as identity comparisons against a caller-supplied handle rather than returning the raw non-owning ma_data_source*; set/get_next_callback via a shim-owned C callback. The 5 ma_data_source_node_* functions init against an engine's node graph. 17 binding + 19 API tests on the null backend (sample round-trip, seek-rewind equivalence, range restriction, buffer-ownership-after-caller-drop).

ring_buffer.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 38 of 38 functions bound, 0 excluded. Two lock-free SPSC ring buffers, both purely in-memory (no device, engine, or file): ma_rb (untyped, bytes) via a RingBuffer RAII type and ma_pcm_rb (PCM-aware, frames) via PcmRingBuffer. miniaudio's acquire/commit pair hands out an interior pointer into the ring that Mojo has no safe home for, so the shim owns the acquire -> memcpy -> commit loop and exposes copy-in/copy-out write/read instead; the loop stitches requests that span the wrap point back together, so acquire_read/acquire_write/commit_read/commit_write are bound through it. get_subbuffer_ptr returns an absolute address, bound as that pointer's byte offset from the ring's own backing store (the only part Mojo can assert on) -- note the pcm variant's offset is frame-valued while its ptr offset is byte-valued, matching miniaudio. init_ex covers both the miniaudio-owned allocation (requested stride ignored in favour of a SIMD-aligned one) and the preallocated path (stride honoured) with a shim-owned backing store. 24 binding + 18 API tests (byte and frame round-trips, wrap-point contiguity, short write at capacity / short read when empty, available_read+available_write==subbuffer_size invariant, seek_read/seek_write, and a 100-frame producer/consumer stream through a 16-frame ring).

channel_converter.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 8 of 8 functions bound, 0 excluded. Channel count / channel map conversion, with NULL channel maps asking miniaudio for its standard map at each count. Both init paths covered (managed heap and shim-owned preallocated heap, asserted to convert identically). Two upstream behaviours are pinned by tests: a mono *output* always takes miniaudio's averaging fast path regardless of the mix mode, and init validates channel counts but not the sample format (an unknown format is accepted). 10 binding + 9 API tests.

data_converter.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 16 of 16 functions bound, 0 excluded. Format + channels + rate in one pipeline. Three construction paths: init, init_preallocated (shim-owned heap), and a config_init_default path that starts from miniaudio's defaults and only overrides the pass-through shape, so the defaults stay observable. Pins an upstream limitation of ma_data_converter_reset in miniaudio 0.11.25: it resets the resampler but does not restore a cold pipeline -- a fresh converter low-passes the first frames (0, 0.7921, 2.7399, ...) while the same converter after a reset returns the unfiltered interpolation (0, 1.0, 3.0, ...). Confirmed against raw miniaudio with a standalone C probe; the bare ma_resampler does not show it. Rebuild rather than reset when bit-identical restarts matter. 11 binding + 11 API tests.

resampler.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 13 of 13 functions bound, 0 excluded. A pure DSP object -- no device, engine, or file. Both init paths are covered: init (miniaudio owns the working heap) and get_heap_size + init_preallocated (the shim owns it), with a test asserting the two produce identical audio. process passes the input and output frame counts by reference, so they go in as requests and come back as actuals; the tests pin that against the converter's own get_expected_output_frame_count rather than hard-coded numbers. Note that set_rate_ratio takes miniaudio's ratioInOut -- input over output -- so 2.0 halves the rate; the L3 docstring says so and a test pins it. 10 binding + 10 API tests.

waveform.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 9 MA_API functions bound (config_init/init/uninit/read_pcm_frames/seek_to_pcm_frame/set_amplitude/set_frequency/set_type/set_sample_rate). 8 binding tests + 7 API tests (silence, amplitude change, seek-restart, stereo).

noise.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 6 bindable of 9 functions bound (config_init+init/uninit/read_pcm_frames/set_amplitude/set_seed). set_type excluded (deprecated, asserts false in miniaudio). get_heap_size/init_preallocated excluded (internal allocator helpers). 8 binding tests + 7 API tests (white/pink/brownian, amplitude change, stereo).

biquad.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 13 of 13 functions bound, 0 excluded. The raw biquad plus its node-graph variant. Pure DSP -- the filter needs nothing, and the node only needs an engine on the null backend. Both init paths are bound (managed heap, and get_heap_size + init_preallocated with a shim-owned block) and asserted to filter identically. Behaviour is pinned with the identity coefficients (b0=1, rest 0), which pass audio through untouched, so the tests do not depend on any particular filter response. ma_biquad_clear_cache correctly zeroes the delay registers, unlike ma_lpf1_clear_cache -- see the lpf notes. 10 binding + 8 API tests.

sync.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 24 of 24 functions bound, 0 excluded. Mutex, event, semaphore, fence and both async notification shapes, all plain in-memory primitives. Every waiting call is bound and exercised -- always after a signal, a release, or on a fence already back at zero, so nothing blocks the test thread. Pins an upstream bug in miniaudio 0.11.25: ma_async_notification_signal fires the notification's callback and then returns MA_INVALID_ARGS -- its success path returns an error code. The signal itself lands, which the is_signalled check proves, so the raw layer reports the code unchanged while AsyncPoll.signal absorbs it; raising there would make the call unusable for the one thing it does. 6 binding + 6 API tests.

log.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 9 of 9 functions bound, 0 excluded. A log callback has to be a C function, so the shim owns one that counts the messages it is handed -- that count is how Mojo observes registration, posting and unregistration taking effect. ma_log_postv takes a va_list, which the shim builds in a variadic wrapper forwarding one string argument, so all three posting shapes (post / postf / postv) are reachable. 5 binding + 5 API tests.

context.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 9 of 9 functions bound, 0 excluded. The context is built on the null backend, so enumeration returns miniaudio's synthetic devices and no hardware is touched. Three calls hand back things Mojo cannot hold and are bound as what can safely cross: ma_context_enumerate_devices takes a callback, so the shim owns one that counts what it is offered; ma_context_get_devices hands back arrays the context owns, so only their lengths cross; ma_context_get_log binds as whether a log is present. A test asserts the enumeration count equals the two array lengths added together, which is the invariant tying those two bindings together. 5 binding + 5 API tests.

vfs.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 16 bindable of 19 functions bound; the 3 _w wide-char variants are excluded project-wide. Wraps miniaudio's default (stdio) VFS. ma_vfs_file is an opaque pointer with no safe Mojo home, so an open file lives in a slot on the handle. Both entry-point families are bound: the plain ma_vfs_* calls against the shim's own VFS, and the ma_vfs_or_default_* calls with a NULL VFS, which is the fallback those functions exist for -- they get a second, independent slot. The ma_vfs_or_default_* family is exported by miniaudio but absent from its public header, so the shim declares it rather than leaving it unbound. Tests write their own fixture under build/ and assert a byte-for-byte round trip. 6 binding + 6 API tests.

audio_buffer.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 25 of 25 functions bound, 0 excluded. Two in-memory PCM buffers, no device/engine/file involved: ma_audio_buffer_ref (a non-owning view) via an AudioBufferRef RAII type and ma_audio_buffer (owning) via AudioBuffer. ref_init / ref_set_data and the non-copying audio_buffer_init all store the caller's pointer verbatim, which no Mojo value can safely outlive across FFI calls, so the shim holds its own copy of the frames and hands miniaudio that -- the same ownership move the data_source family makes. map/unmap hand out an interior pointer with no safe Mojo home, so the shim owns the map -> memcpy -> unmap sequence and binds both through a *_map_read entry point that surfaces unmap's MA_AT_END (a success) verbatim. All four construction paths are covered: init (shim-owned frames), init_copy (miniaudio allocates and copies), init_copy with a NULL source (silence), and alloc_and_init (heap ma_audio_buffer with the frames in its trailing _pExtraData, torn down via uninit_and_free). alloc_and_init is bound as-is despite an upstream defect in miniaudio 0.11.25: it copies the frames before init_ex runs, and init_ex's MA_ZERO_MEMORY(p, sizeof(*p) - sizeof(p->_pExtraData)) overshoots into the audio data by the struct's trailing padding, clearing the low 3 bytes of frame 0 (an f32 20.0 reads back as 8.0). The binding test pins that behaviour so a future upstream fix fails loudly. 17 binding + 16 API tests (frame-ordered round trips, frames-not-samples accounting for stereo, the available==length-cursor invariant across seeks, looping reads that wrap, map_read agreeing with read chunk for chunk, and rejection of empty/zero-frame buffers on every init path).

paged_audio_buffer.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 16 of 16 functions bound, 0 excluded. An expandable linked list of PCM pages plus a reader that walks it, purely in-memory. One shim handle owns both halves (the ma_paged_audio_buffer_data list and the ma_paged_audio_buffer reader) while keeping miniaudio's lifetime split: data_init/data_uninit manage the pages, init/uninit manage the reader. Pages are ma_paged_audio_buffer_page* values with no safe Mojo home, so data_allocate_page parks the page in a slot on the handle and returns the slot index, which data_append_page / data_free_page take back; slots still holding a page at teardown are released with it, so an allocate with no matching append/free cannot leak. data_get_head / data_get_tail return raw page pointers and are bound as the properties Mojo can assert on -- the page's frame count plus whether the list is still empty (head is a zero-length dummy and the tail starts out pointing at it). Note that read_pcm_frames returns MA_AT_END whenever the read consumes the final page, even when every requested frame arrived; the L3 layer treats that as the success miniaudio documents it to be. 13 binding + 11 API tests (multi-page contiguous reads, the live-append property -- a page added after the reader drained is picked up -- the two-step vs one-step append agreeing, staged pages discarded without joining the stream, seeks landing mid-list, and frames-not-samples accounting).

lpf.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 31 of 31 functions bound, 0 excluded. The first-order ma_lpf1, the second-order ma_lpf2, the compound ma_lpf and ma_lpf_node. Behaviour is asserted the way a low-pass is defined -- DC survives, a signal alternating every frame does not -- rather than against hard-coded coefficients. Pins an upstream bug in miniaudio 0.11.25: ma_lpf1_clear_cache zeroes the filter *coefficient* (`a`) instead of the delay register (`pR1`), so it de-tunes the filter into a pass-through rather than clearing it; ma_biquad_clear_cache zeroes pR1/pR2 correctly. The compound ma_lpf inherits this through its first-order section, so reinit after clear_cache. Also deliberately does not assert that a higher order attenuates more: measured at the alternating signal, order 4 settles around 1.5e-3 and order 2 around 1e-4. 12 binding + 9 API tests.

hpf.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 28 of 28 functions bound, 0 excluded. The first-order ma_hpf1, the second-order ma_hpf2, the compound ma_hpf and ma_hpf_node. miniaudio gives the high-pass family no clear_cache entry point, so none is bound. Pins what ma_hpf1 actually is: its recursion is y = b*x - a*r1 with a = 1 - alpha and b = alpha (alpha being the same pole coefficient ma_lpf1 stores), giving a DC gain of alpha/(2-alpha) and a Nyquist gain of 1 -- at cutoff 1 kHz and 48 kHz that is ~0.781 at DC, a gentle shelf rather than a true high-pass. ma_hpf2 and the even-order compound ma_hpf are biquad-based and do reject DC. 11 binding + 9 API tests.

bpf.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 20 of 20 functions bound, 0 excluded. The second-order ma_bpf2, the compound ma_bpf and ma_bpf_node. Same shim, same X-macro-generated lifecycle and the same two init paths as the biquad / lpf / hpf batch (managed heap, and get_heap_size + init_preallocated with a shim-owned block, asserted to filter identically). No clear_cache exists upstream for this family. Behaviour is asserted by what defines a band-pass: it rejects both extremes, so DC and a signal alternating every frame both settle below 1e-3. 8 binding + 13 API tests.

notch.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 12 of 12 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_notch2 and ma_notch_node. Same shim, same X-macro-generated lifecycle and the same two init paths as the biquad / lpf / hpf batch (managed heap, and get_heap_size + init_preallocated with a shim-owned block, asserted to filter identically). No clear_cache exists upstream for this family. Behaviour is asserted by what defines a notch: it removes one narrow band and leaves the rest alone, so with the notch at 1 kHz both DC and the fastest signal come back at unity gain. 5 binding + 7 API tests.

peak_eq.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 12 of 12 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_peak2 and ma_peak_node. Same shim, same X-macro-generated lifecycle and the same two init paths as the biquad / lpf / hpf batch (managed heap, and get_heap_size + init_preallocated with a shim-owned block, asserted to filter identically). No clear_cache exists upstream for this family. Behaviour is pinned with a 0 dB band, which is exactly transparent, so the test does not depend on the shape of the bell. 5 binding + 7 API tests.

loshelf.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 12 of 12 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_loshelf2 and ma_loshelf_node. Same shim, same X-macro-generated lifecycle and the same two init paths as the biquad / lpf / hpf batch (managed heap, and get_heap_size + init_preallocated with a shim-owned block, asserted to filter identically). No clear_cache exists upstream for this family. Behaviour is pinned numerically: +12 dB below 1 kHz gives a measured DC gain of 3.981, which is 10^(12/20), against a gain of 1.0 at the fastest signal. Note miniaudio tunes the shelf *node* by q where the standalone shelf filter takes a shelf slope; the API keeps that asymmetry rather than hiding it. 5 binding + 7 API tests.

hishelf.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 12 of 12 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_hishelf2 and ma_hishelf_node -- the mirror image of the low shelf, with the measured 3.981 gain landing on the fastest signal and 1.0 on DC. Same shim, same X-macro-generated lifecycle and the same two init paths as the biquad / lpf / hpf batch (managed heap, and get_heap_size + init_preallocated with a shim-owned block, asserted to filter identically). No clear_cache exists upstream for this family. The same node-tuned-by-q asymmetry applies. 5 binding + 7 API tests.

node_graph.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 9 of 9 functions bound, 0 excluded. The graph is created standalone -- no device and no engine -- so reading it is a pure computation. ma_node_graph_get_endpoint hands out a raw pointer with no safe Mojo home, so it is bound as what the endpoint can be asked (its input bus count) and as the attach target for the node families. Pins that an empty graph reads zero frames rather than manufacturing silence, and that the clock only advances once something is attached. 6 binding + 4 API tests.

delay_node.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 9 of 9 functions bound, 0 excluded. Exercised inside a standalone graph, fed by the shim's offset node. Pins what miniaudio's delay actually does with dry and wet, which is not the effects-mixer blend the names suggest: the implementation is buffer = buffer*decay + in*dry, out = buffer*wet, so dry is the gain going into the delay line and wet is the gain of the node's whole output. There is no separate un-delayed path -- wet=0 silences the node whatever dry is, and the immediate signal comes out scaled by dry*wet (measured: 1x1 gives 0.4 from a 0.4 input, 0.5x0.5 gives 0.1). 5 binding + 4 API tests.

splitter_node.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 3 of 3 functions bound, 0 excluded. One input, two identical outputs; attaching both output buses to the endpoint sums the signal with itself, which is how the test shows both buses carry the same audio. 4 binding + 3 API tests.

job_queue.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 9 of 9 functions bound, 0 excluded. ma_job has no safe Mojo home, so the queue works through a single job slot the shim keeps: post builds and queues a job of a given type code, next pops one into the slot and reports its type, process runs what is in the slot. Both init paths are covered. A quit job comes back labelled MA_CANCELLED from next, which is the label rather than a failure. 4 binding + 4 API tests.

slot_allocator.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 7 of 7 functions bound, 0 excluded. The lock-free slot allocator behind the job queue, with both init paths covered and distinct slots asserted across two claims. 4 binding + 3 API tests.

linear_resampler.notes: L1+L2+L3 COMPLETE: all 13 of 13 functions bound, 0 excluded. The algorithm ma_resampler drives underneath when set to linear, bound in its own right with the same shape minus the algorithm selector, and sharing the converter shim. Both init paths are covered and asserted to produce identical audio. The strongest test compares it directly against ma_resampler configured for linear at the same rates: the two agree frame for frame, which is what makes binding both meaningful rather than redundant. Unlike ma_data_converter, its reset does restore a cold run. 8 binding + 7 API tests.
